# -set-alias semantics

Scratch dir with all reproducers: `/tmp/probe/set-alias/`
Runner used for every experiment (`/tmp/probe/set-alias/bin/run.sh`):

```sh
#!/bin/sh
# usage: run.sh <workdir> <outprefix> [args...]
WD="$1"; shift
PFX="$1"; shift
export GOPROXY=off
export GOFLAGS=-mod=mod
export GOTOOLCHAIN=local
cd "$WD" || exit 99
/workspace/executable "$@" >"$PFX.out" 2>"$PFX.err"
echo $? > "$PFX.code"
```

All commands below were executed with cwd = the module root shown, `GOPROXY=off`,
`GOFLAGS=-mod=mod`, `GOTOOLCHAIN=local`. Log timestamps in real bytes use **slashes**
(`2026/08/10 14:15:00`); they are rendered with dashes in some terminals. Verified with `od -c`.

---

## TL;DR of the rule

`-set-alias` adds `name ` in front of an import path **iff**

1. the import spec has **no** name/alias at all (no identifier, no `_`, no `.`), **and**
2. the *loaded* package's `package` clause name **!=** `path.Base(importPath)` (byte-exact,
   case-sensitive comparison).

The alias inserted is the **real package clause name** obtained from the Go tool, never
anything derived from the path. It is **not** about version suffixes at all — `/vN` just happens
to be the most common way to make `Base(path) != packageName`.

Existing names are **never** changed, never removed, never validated. No de-duplication.

---

## Confirmed behaviors

### 1. Alias is the loaded package's real name, not path-derived

Module `/tmp/probe/set-alias/m1`:

```
go.mod:        module example.com/proj \n\n go 1.21
pg/v9/pg.go:   package pgsql \n\n func Hello() {}
simple/v2/s.go:package simple \n\n func Hello() {}
a.go:
        package main

        import (
                "fmt"

                "example.com/proj/pg/v9"
                "example.com/proj/simple/v2"
        )

        func main() {
                fmt.Println(pgsql.Hello, simple.Hello)
        }
```

Command: `executable -set-alias -output stdout a.go`
exit **0**

stdout (`cat -A`, `^I` = TAB, `$` = EOL):
```
package main$
$
import ($
^I"fmt"$
$
^Ipgsql "example.com/proj/pg/v9"$
^Isimple "example.com/proj/simple/v2"$
)$
$
func main() {$
^Ifmt.Println(pgsql.Hello, simple.Hello)$
}$
```
stderr:
```
2026/08/10 14:15:00 Paths: [a.go]
2026/08/10 14:15:00 Processing a.go
```

`pg/v9` → `pgsql` (not `pg`): the alias comes from the package clause.

### 2. Matrix: which import paths get an alias (module `/tmp/probe/set-alias/m2`)

Each row = a separate file `test/tNN/a.go` in package `tNN` of module `example.com/proj`,
shaped:
```go
package tNN

import (
	"fmt"

	"<IMPORT PATH>"
)

var _ = fmt.Sprint
var _ = <PKGNAME>.F
```
Command per row: `executable -set-alias -output stdout test/tNN/a.go` (exit 0 for all rows).

| import path | package clause | `path.Base` | result import line |
|---|---|---|---|
| `example.com/proj/lib/v0` | `lib` | `v0` | `lib "example.com/proj/lib/v0"` |
| `example.com/proj/lib/v1` | `lib` | `v1` | `lib "example.com/proj/lib/v1"` |
| `example.com/proj/lib/v2` | `lib` | `v2` | `lib "example.com/proj/lib/v2"` |
| `example.com/proj/lib/v10` | `lib` | `v10` | `lib "example.com/proj/lib/v10"` |
| `example.com/proj/lib/vX` | `lib` | `vX` | `lib "example.com/proj/lib/vX"` |
| `example.com/proj/lib/v2.1` | `lib` | `v2.1` | `lib "example.com/proj/lib/v2.1"` |
| `example.com/proj/libu/V2` | `lib` | `V2` | `lib "example.com/proj/libu/V2"` |
| `example.com/proj/lib/v` | `lib` | `v` | `lib "example.com/proj/lib/v"` |
| `example.com/proj/lib/v1beta1` | `lib` | `v1beta1` | `lib "example.com/proj/lib/v1beta1"` |
| `example.com/proj/foo/v2/bar` | `bar` | `bar` | `"example.com/proj/foo/v2/bar"` (**no alias**; `v2` mid-path is irrelevant) |
| `example.com/proj/yaml.v2` | `yaml` | `yaml.v2` | `yaml "example.com/proj/yaml.v2"` |
| `example.com/proj/foo-go` | `foo` | `foo-go` | `foo "example.com/proj/foo-go"` (**non-versioned, aliased**) |
| `example.com/proj/mismatch` | `other` | `mismatch` | `other "example.com/proj/mismatch"` |

Decisive negative case (module `/tmp/probe/set-alias/m3`, file `test/u01/a.go`,

`executable -set-alias -output stdout test/u01/a.go` → exit 0, stdout import block:
```
import ($
^I"fmt"$
$
^I"example.com/proj/pgA/v9"$
)$
```
**No alias**, even though the path ends in `/v9`. This kills the "alias versioned paths" theory
and the "strip the version then compare" theory (which would have compared `pgA` vs `v9` and
aliased). Together with `lib/v2` → `lib "…/lib/v2"` above, the comparison is provably
`pkgName != path.Base(importPath)`.

Case sensitivity (`/tmp/probe/set-alias/fZ`, dir `Foo` containing `package foo`):
`executable -set-alias -output stdout a.go` → `foo "example.com/proj/Foo"` (aliased ⇒ compare is
case-sensitive).

Single-segment import path (`/tmp/probe/set-alias/m12`: `replace single => ./sub/single`,
`sub/single/x.go` = `package other`):
```
input:   f "fmt" / _ "os" / "single"
output:  f "fmt"$   _ "os"$   (blank)   other "single"$
```
Module-root import (`/tmp/probe/set-alias/m16`, `root.go` = `package root` at module root):
`"example.com/proj"` → `root "example.com/proj"` (Base = `proj`).

Canonical README case (`/tmp/probe/set-alias/m14`,
`replace github.com/go-pg/pg/v9 => ./sub/pg`, `sub/pg/x.go` = `package pg`):
`"github.com/go-pg/pg/v9"` → `pg "github.com/go-pg/pg/v9"`. ✔ matches README.

`gopkg.in`-style (`/tmp/probe/set-alias/m4`, `replace gopkg.in/yaml.v2 => ./sub/yaml`,
`package yaml`): `"gopkg.in/yaml.v2"` → `yaml "gopkg.in/yaml.v2"` (Base `yaml.v2` != `yaml`).
So yes, an alias IS added even when the last *non-version* part already equals the package name.

Third-party/general group also aliased (`m4`, `replace github.com/foo/bar/v3 => ./sub/bar`,
`package barpkg`): `barpkg "github.com/foo/bar/v3"`.

### 3. Existing names are never touched (module `/tmp/probe/set-alias/m3`)

`plain/x.go` = `package plain` (Base matches), `odd/x.go` = `package weird` (Base mismatches).
Command per row `executable -set-alias -output stdout test/uNN/a.go`, exit 0 for all.

| file | input import line | output import line |
|---|---|---|
| u03 | `zzz "example.com/proj/plain"` | `zzz "example.com/proj/plain"` (unchanged) |
| u04 | `zzz "example.com/proj/odd"` | `zzz "example.com/proj/odd"` (**not** rewritten to `weird`) |
| u05 | `weird "example.com/proj/odd"` | `weird "example.com/proj/odd"` |
| u06 | `plain "example.com/proj/plain"` | `plain "example.com/proj/plain"` (redundant alias **kept**) |
| u07 | `_ "example.com/proj/odd"` | `_ "example.com/proj/odd"` |
| u08 | `. "example.com/proj/odd"` | `. "example.com/proj/odd"` |
| u10 | `zzz "example.com/proj/pgB/v9"` (`package pgB`) | `zzz "example.com/proj/pgB/v9"` |
| u02 | `"example.com/proj/pgB/v9"` | `pgB "example.com/proj/pgB/v9"` |

So: no alias removal, no alias rewriting, no alias validation. Blank (`_`) and dot (`.`) imports
count as "already named" and are left alone.

`f "fmt"` and `_ "os"` survive untouched too (m12).

### 4. std imports

`/tmp/probe/set-alias/m3/test/u09/a.go` importing `"fmt"`, `"math/rand"`, `"os/exec"`:
`executable -set-alias -output stdout test/u09/a.go` → exit 0, block unchanged:
```
import ($
^I"fmt"$
^I"math/rand"$
^I"os/exec"$
)$
```
No std package in go1.21 has `Name != Base` except `runtime/internal/wasitest` (unimportable), so
I could not prove whether std is *specially excluded* or merely never mismatched — see
Open questions. `import "C"` (cgo) is left alone (`/tmp/probe/set-alias/hA`, exit 0).

### 5. Idempotency and `-output`

Module `/tmp/probe/set-alias/m5` (`odd`=`package weird`, `plain`=`package plain`), `a.go`:
```go
package main

import (
	"fmt"
	"example.com/proj/odd"
	"example.com/proj/plain"
)

func main() { fmt.Println(weird.F, plain.F) }
```

```

$

^I"fmt"$
$
^Iweird "example.com/proj/odd"$
^I"example.com/proj/plain"$
)$
$
func main() { fmt.Println(weird.F, plain.F) }$
```

```

p g s q l   " e x a m p l e . c o m / p r o j / p g / v 9 " \n ) \n \n
f u n c   m a i n ( )   {   f m t . P r i n t l n ( p g s q l . F )   } \n
```

## Exact strings / formats

All log lines go to **stderr** through Go's `log` with default flags:
`YYYY/MM/DD HH:MM:SS ` prefix (space separator, `\n` terminator).

```
<TS> Paths: [<TARGET>]
<TS> Processing <TARGET>
<TS> Failed to fix file: package has an errors
<TS> Failed to fix directory <TARGET>: failed to walk dif: failed to fix <ABS_FILE_PATH>: package has an errors
<TS> Failed to fix file: file has invalid Go source content, use -excludes flag to skip this file: <ABS_FILE>:<LINE>:<COL>: <PARSER MSG>
<TS> Failed to fix file: err: exit status 1: stderr: go: go.mod file not found in current directory or any parent directory; see 'go help modules'\n\n
<TS> Failed to fix file: err: go command required, not found: exec: "go": executable file not found in $PATH: stderr: \n
```

Notes verified with `od -c`:
* `failed to walk dif:` — **typo in the binary** ("dif", not "diff"). Byte sequence:
  `F a i l e d   t o   f i x   d i r e c t o r y   . / . . . :   f a i l e d   t o   w a l k   d i f :   f a i l e d   t o   f i x   / t m p / … / c . g o :   p a c k a g e   h a s   a n   e r r o r s \n`
* the `go.mod`-missing message ends with `'go help modules'\n\n` (the go tool's own newline is kept, then `log` adds one).
* the missing-`go` message ends with `stderr: \n` (trailing space, empty stderr).
* `package has an errors` — ungrammatical, verbatim.

Raw go-tool diagnostics are printed to stderr **without** a log timestamp, one per line, e.g.
```
<FILE>:<LINE>:<COL>: cannot find module providing package <PATH>: module lookup disabled by GOPROXY=off
<FILE>:<LINE>:<COL>: found packages <NAME1> (<FILE1>) and <NAME2> (<FILE2>) in <ABS_DIR>
<FILE>:<LINE>:<COL>: import "<PATH>" is a program, not an importable package
-: import cycle not allowed: import stack: [<PATH> <PATH> …]
-: no Go files in
-: <FILE>: multiple //go:build comments
```
`-: no Go files in` is byte-exact and has **no** directory after "in" and no trailing space
(`… f i l e s   i n \n`), even when the package is in a subdirectory
(`/tmp/probe/set-alias/fI3`, target `sub/a.go`). Contrast the go tool's own wording, which would
be `build constraints exclude all Go files in /abs/dir` — so this text is produced by the loader
layer, not copied from `go list`.

Emitted import line format: `\t` + optional `<alias>` + `" "` + `"` + path + `"` (exactly one
space between alias and the quoted path), then any trailing comment as ` // …`
(`/tmp/probe/set-alias/fK`: `^Iweird "example.com/proj/odd" // my comment$`).
For an unparenthesised single import the whole decl is rewritten:
`/tmp/probe/set-alias/fJ` input `import "example.com/proj/odd"` → output
`import weird "example.com/proj/odd"`. Two separate `import` decls are merged into one
parenthesised block (`/tmp/probe/set-alias/hC`).

## Algorithm inference

```
fixFile(path, flags):
  src   := read(path)
  file  := parse(path, src)                      # parse errors -> "file has invalid Go source content…"
  if isGenerated(file) and not applyToGeneratedFiles: return src unchanged   # BEFORE any loading
  if excluded(path):                             return src unchanged        # BEFORE any loading

  aliases := map[string]string{}                 # importPath -> package clause name
  if flags.setAlias or flags.rmUnused:
      tags := extractBuildTags(file)             # see below
      pkg, errs := loadPackage(dir(path), tags)  # go/packages, Tests: true, via the `go` tool
      printAll(errs -> stderr, no timestamp)     # every error in the loaded graph
      if rootHasErrors(pkg) and len(tags) > 0:
          pkg, errs = loadPackage(dir(path), nil)    # RETRY WITHOUT TAGS
          printAll(errs -> stderr)
      if rootHasErrors(pkg):
          return error("package has an errors")  # -> log "Failed to fix file: package has an errors", exit 1
      for p in pkg.Imports (recursively/whatever the loader provides):
          aliases[p.PkgPath] = p.Name

  # ... unused-import removal (if -rm-unused) ...

  if flags.setAlias:
      for spec in file.Imports:
          if spec.Name != nil: continue                 # keeps identifiers, `_` and `.`
          key := strings.Trim(spec.Path.Value, `"`)     # NOTE: backticks/escapes never match
          name, ok := aliases[key]
          if !ok: continue                             # silently skip (unknown / file not in pkg)
          if name != path.Base(key):                   # byte comparison, case sensitive
              spec.Name = ident(name)                  # no collision check, no validity check

  # ... grouping/sorting/printing ...
```

`extractBuildTags(file)`:
```
line := the single `//go:build …` comment that appears before the package clause  (or "")
tags := []
for tok in strings.Fields(line-after-"//go:build"):
    if tok is a bare build-tag identifier ([A-Za-z0-9_.]+, i.e. no ! ( ) & | ): tags = append(tags, tok)
return tags        # passed as -tags to the go tool
```

Alias decision, restated for a reimplementer:

```
addAlias(importPath, loadedPkgName, existingName) =
    existingName == ""  &&  loadedPkgName != path.Base(importPath)
alias = loadedPkgName
```

## Surprises / gotchas

1. **It is a "mismatch" rule, not a "version" rule.** `foo-go` → `foo`, `mismatch` → `other`,
   `Foo` → `foo`, `example.com/proj` → `root` all get aliases with no version segment anywhere.
   Conversely `pgA/v9` with `package v9` gets **no** alias despite the `/v9`. The README's
   "Set alias for versioned package names" is misleading.
2. **Existing aliases are never corrected.** `zzz "…/odd"` stays `zzz` even though the package is
   `weird`. Redundant aliases (`plain "…/plain"`) are kept.
3. **No collision handling** — two mismatched paths with the same package name both get the same
   alias, producing code that does not compile (module `m16`).
4. **Type errors do not block**, but any *package-resolution* error anywhere in the loaded graph
   (including in sibling `_test.go` files!) aborts with `package has an errors`, exit 1.
   A broken `a_test.go` breaks the run for `a.go`.
5. **The loader runs even when the file has no imports**, so `-set-alias` can fail on a file it
   would never have modified.
6. **Build tags from the target file are fed to the go tool**, and there is a silent
   **retry without tags**. If the retried load excludes the target file, `-set-alias` becomes a
   silent no-op with exit 0 while dozens of go-tool errors are printed to stderr
   (`hB`, `fI`, `mA`, `mC`).
7. **Build-tag tokenisation is naive**: whitespace-split, keep bare identifiers.
   `(foo || bar) && !ignore` and `foo&&ignore` yield **no** tags; `foo && ignore` yields both.
   `//go:build ignore` is actively harmful because `-tags ignore` breaks the go1.21 stdlib.
8. Only `//go:build` is understood; a file with just `// +build foo` fails with `-: no Go files in`.
9. **Raw-string / escaped import paths** are re-quoted but never aliased.
10. Generated files (`// Code generated` first comment) are returned **byte-identical** — no
    sorting, no formatting — and skip the load entirely.
11. `-set-exit-status` returns 1 when the only change is the added alias.
12. `-separate-named` and `-set-alias` compose: a freshly added alias moves the import into the
    named block.
13. `-set-alias` with `-recursive`/`./...` aborts the whole walk on the first failing file, but
    files already processed (walk order is lexical) are **already written**
    (`m9`: `p1/a.go` fixed, then `p2/c.go` failed, exit 1).
14. The error text `package has an errors` and the directory-mode `failed to walk dif` typo must
    be reproduced verbatim.
